cut_items.item: Redis without AOF can lose queued jobs on restart (shared with Y's AOF warning, but X frames restart)
Redis/BullMQ offers job flows and very low latency (flows specifically)
Moving to BullMQ later is easy if handlers are plain functions (Y has similar advice)
Explicit warning not to write your own queue

added_items.item: Set Redis maxmemory-policy noeviction, otherwise queued jobs can be silently evicted
Postgres queue churn causes table bloat; keep autovacuum healthy and delete old completed jobs
Long-running workers hold connections; size the connection pool accordingly
Heavy job traffic can slow main queries when sharing one database
Redis offloads job load from the main database
BullMQ features: repeatable jobs, priorities, dashboard, delayed jobs
pg-boss/graphile-worker support retries, scheduling, delayed jobs
Explains SKIP LOCKED lets many workers claim different rows without blocking
Redis enqueue is not transactional with a Postgres write: if write succeeds and enqueue fails, job is lost
Explicit numeric decision rule (~1,000 jobs/sec threshold for BullMQ)
AOF explained as append-only log
Postgres risk: queue churn creates dead rows/table bloat; keep autovacuum healthy and delete old completed jobs
Postgres risk: long-running workers hold connections; size the connection pool accordingly
Postgres risk: heavy job traffic can slow main queries when sharing one database
Redis must set maxmemory-policy noeviction, otherwise queued jobs can be silently evicted
Redis cannot enqueue in the same transaction as a Postgres write; a successful write with a failed enqueue loses the job
Explains that SKIP LOCKED lets many workers claim different rows without blocking
Postgres handles thousands of jobs/sec with SKIP LOCKED, and the switch threshold is about 1,000 jobs/sec
Redis advantage: jobs add no load to the main database
BullMQ features: delayed and repeatable jobs, priorities, dashboard
Library features: pg-boss and graphile-worker support retries, scheduling, and delayed jobs
Explains AOF as an append-only log on disk
